newsitem.title: SPAIN: New Spanish regional airline start up.
newsitem.headline: New Spanish regional airline start up.

text.p: A new Spanish regional carrier, 50 percent owned by Air Europa, started operations last month with two British Aerospace ATP aircraft under the name Air Europa Express, managing director Mario Hidalgo said.
The airline, originally to be called Canarias Regional Air, will act as a feeder for Air Europa's longer range services.
It already has firm orders for eight aircraft and is likely to order five more, Hidalgo told Reuters.
It is discussing the possibility of buying some of them rather than leasing.

So far it is flying two aircraft on routes between the Balearic Islands and mainland cities such as Barcelona, Valladolid and Valencia. A third aircraft is being used for crew training and numbers four and five are due to arrive later this week.
It has been unable to start services from Madrid as planned because of the impossibility of obtaining take off and landing slots at the capital's already saturated Barajas airport.

"If not for the slot problem we would have started by now," Hidalgo said, adding the company was studying the feasibility of using the former U.S. air base at Torrejon as an alternative to Barajas if the government decides to open it to commercial flights to relieve overcrowding at the main airport.
Services from the Canary Islands, which were to have been the new airline's base, are now unlikely to start until March or April next year, Hidalgo said.
Air Europa, majority-owned by the Hidalgo family, has an extensive network of domestic routes and runs international scheduled flights to London, New York and Mexico.
It is also negotiating flying to Argentina and Chile. --Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44-171-542-7706 Fax +171-171-542-5017
